summary: This bill directs the Secretary of Commerce to report within 270 days on national security risks to the U.S. electric grid from foreign adversary-controlled apps that remotely operate high-wattage IoT devices such as smart appliances, including recommendations to restrict such apps, and codifies Executive Order 13873 on the ICTS supply chain.

scores.thoughts: The bill requires the Secretary of Commerce to produce a report and codifies an existing executive order. No new appropriations, spending authorizations, or cuts are specified or implied.
No provisions address taxes, tax rates, or revenue measures of any kind.
The legislation concerns electric-grid security and IoT devices; it has no bearing on healthcare delivery, coverage, or markets.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues appear in the text.
The bill does not address immigration policy, visas, border enforcement, or pathways to citizenship.
No provisions relate to reproductive health services or abortion access.
While framed in national-security terms, the bill neither authorizes nor reduces military or defense appropriations; its focus is civilian critical infrastructure.
Grid-stability concerns are mentioned, but the legislation does not expand or limit environmental regulations, emissions standards, or conservation measures.
No welfare, entitlement, or social-services programs are created, modified, or addressed.
The bill contains no education funding, school-choice, or federal-education-policy provisions.
No drug-enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance measures are present.
The legislation does not alter sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice procedures.

The bill recommends restrictions on transactions involving foreign-adversary-controlled applications and devices, procurement bans, and supply-chain controls aimed at China and other adversaries. These measures constitute targeted protectionist actions rather than free-trade liberalization.
No deficit, debt-ceiling, or fiscal-balance provisions are included.
The text does not address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil-rights issues.
Foreign-aid funding or policy is not mentioned.
No election-administration, voting-access, or campaign-related measures appear.

The bill directs assessment of data-collection and remote-control risks posed by foreign-adversary apps and recommends mitigation measures including transaction restrictions and certification requirements. This increases federal oversight of specific foreign technology products.
No labor, union, or workplace-regulation provisions are present.
The legislation does not engage religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
